figures.title: Generated traffic on eight held-out scenarios
figures.caption: One seed shown (1900). 10 paired seeds × 120 windows × 8 scenarios; capacities 10 Mbps per path. Demand traces are synthetic and hash-verified.

figures.title: Modeled delay by scenario and controller
figures.caption: 86,400 controller windows, 9,600 unique workload windows. Queue-based fluid delay; no packet RTT or physical-network measurements.

figures.title: A4 versus H1: loss improves, delay has a tradeoff
figures.caption: A4 minus H1 with paired 95% seed bootstrap intervals (4,000 draws). Negative favors A4. Improvements over H1 include capacity-aware meter logic, not only memory.

figures.title: Matched H2 ablation isolates episodic parameter selection
figures.caption: H2 shares the capacity-aware meter and uses a fixed 0.1 Mbps headroom. A4 explores 0, 0.1 and 0.3 Mbps, then selects using observed prior reward. Cold-start exploration stays in results.

figures.title: Delay, loss and delivered goodput together
figures.caption: Equal weight per scenario and seed. All loss includes deliberate meter drops and buffer overflow. H1 and previous v3 A4 match; H2 and A4 differ in parameter selection.

figures.title: Distribution of modeled window outcomes
figures.caption: 9,600 windows per controller, including overload, transitions and cold start. Individual windows within a seed are dependent; these curves are descriptive.

figures.title: Installed actions and independent safety checks
figures.caption: The unchanged safety limits enforce exact target/route, alternate utilization ≤90%, rate reduction ≤20% and minimum meter 512 kbps.

figures.title: Queue response through a traffic distribution shift
figures.caption: Seed 1900 shown. Queues carry between windows; changing a rule does not erase queued traffic. Each intervention expires after five virtual seconds.

figures.title: Actual local computation in the isolated .venv
figures.caption: Per-window time includes selection, safety, fluid outcome, reward and memory update. Final batched memory flush excluded. Local timings depend on this machine and concurrent load.

figures.title: Measured provider integration with five-second traffic arrivals
figures.caption: Two fresh seeds, 24 windows per mode/provider. Observation idle time is separately recorded; all control work, pacing, process startup, cancellation and cleanup is included. Timeouts remain in metrics.

figures.title: Fresh suggestions, local reuse and fallbacks are separate
figures.caption: A provider timeout is a local client deadline, not a successful response. Admission deferrals start no request. No API work is silently moved outside the control interval.

figures.title: Control tail latency with all windows retained
figures.caption: Modes use reversed order on the second seed to reduce order bias. Provider variability remains. A 3.8-second local wait budget leaves time for validation and measurement; it is not a hard real-time OS guarantee.

figures.title: Availability of every discovered zero-price OpenRouter model
figures.caption: 1/17 healthy-network schema checks valid. Zero bar marks unavailable/error, not zero latency. Availability check is separate from network-control quality or provider ranking.

figures.title: Meter parameters retain more traffic than the fixed 80% rule
figures.caption: H2 uses a capacity-fitting meter with 0.1 Mbps headroom. A4 varies headroom through bounded prior-outcome exploration. The safety floor clips all candidates at at least 80% of elephant demand.

figures.title: Episodic learning includes cold-start exploration cost
figures.caption: Primary evaluation, all eight scenarios and ten seeds. Higher reward is better. H2 is the matched no-memory ablation; an A4 advantage over H1 alone cannot prove an extra memory benefit.

figures.title: Complete simulated rule changes: port, meter and expiry
figures.caption: Saved real-provider and fallback decisions drive a simulated OpenFlow table. Exact match, cookie, instructions, meter cap, prior-rule expiry and final default restoration are recorded. No physical switch is contacted.

figures.title: Loss accounting keeps deliberate drops visible
figures.caption: Pooled volume loss differs from the arithmetic mean of window loss reported in primary tables. Conservation: prior queues + offered = delivered + all dropped + final queues.
